rv.q: It might not be enough for this show.
But the play's episodic nature is too much tell, not enough show.
The play feels revelant and lovingly manifest.
Director Will Davis has ensembled a brilliant cast and created an Orlando filled with color, music, laughter, and mystery in a production that can only be described as pure joy.
With intentional casting and whimsical performances, this production will be a treat for audiences.
But the production’s push-and-pull ultimately frustrates.
But the production doesn’t wind up feeling exactly right.
Still, it's hard to escape that this is essentially the live reading of a somewhat condensed novel...

cn.t: Taylor Mac dazzles in this revival of Sarah Ruhl's adaptation of Woolf's gender-fluid classic, but critics find the production uneven—some praise its riotous energy while others feel it doesn't fully capitalize on its timely themes.

vr.q: I anchored myself in admiring the ensemble work here which is super fun and the joy that this cast exudes is just infectious.
